content: {"decision":"Do not use as proposed; redesign and validate before execution.","risks":["Model-generated commands can execute arbitrary code, destroy checkout data, or establish persistence.","Inherited environment and network access enable credential theft, data exfiltration, and unauthorized external actions.","A model reviewer can share failure modes or be manipulated; its approval is not a security boundary.","Harmless-command tests do not establish containment against malicious or accidental behavior."],"required_changes":["Treat generated commands as untrusted. Prefer narrowly scoped operations with validated argument arrays over arbitrary shell execution.","Enforce policy independently of the model, including executable, argument, path, and operation restrictions.","Execute in a disposable, least-privilege sandbox with a sanitized environment, no credentials or host sockets, restricted filesystem access, and network denied by default.","Use an isolated checkout copy, enforce resource and time limits, and record execution and changes.","Require explicit human approval for consequential actions and review changes before applying them to the developer checkout."],"evidence_needed":["Threat model and documented execution boundaries, permissions, and approval rules.","Adversarial tests covering shell injection, traversal, symlink escapes, secret access, exfiltration, persistence, and resource exhaustion.","Independent verification that filesystem, credential, network, and process restrictions hold even when both models approve a harmful command.","Demonstrated fail-closed behavior, audit records, sandbox cleanup, and recovery from interrupted or destructive execution."]}
